Tech Report: The Nightingale First Look: Dakota and Elle Fanning on Their Long-Awaited First Film as Sisters

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when I spoke to Dakota and Elle Fanning last fall, they pondered what it would be like to work and live together while making The Nightingale, the film adaptation of Kristin Hannah’s best-selling novel about French sisters in Nazi-occupied France.
  • Now, more than a year later, the Fanning sisters tell me they needn’t have worried.
  • Hollywood has long been plotting to get the Fanning sisters in the same movie—and not as different versions of the same character, as they played in Dakota’s 2001 feature debut, I Am Sam.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when I spoke to Dakota and Elle Fanning last fall, they pondered what it would be like to work and live together while making The Nightingale, the film adaptation of Kristin Hannah’s best-selling novel about French sisters in Nazi-occupied France. It marks the siblings’ first time acting opposite each other onscreen. “We’ve literally never done a scene together, ever,” Dakota mentioned then, as Elle wondered if she’d get through their first take without breaking character: “Am I going to laugh? Better to get it out of your system now.”.

Now, more than a year later, the Fanning sisters tell me they needn’t have worried. “It was nerve-wracking to think, ‘How is this going to feel?’” states Dakota, who’s in Fresh York to shoot an Apple TV series opposite Elle’s former Sentimental Value costar Stellan Skarsgård. “Our way of processing things that we’re both nervous about is to just not talk about it in an effort to downplay what could go wrong or be strange. So that’s what we did—and it was the easiest thing in the world. We played together our entire lives and acted out scenarios, so it felt like clicking back into that. Like, ‘Oh, of course, this is what we do.’”.

Hollywood has long been plotting to get the Fanning sisters in the same movie—and not as different versions of the same character, as they played in Dakota’s 2001 feature debut, I Am Sam. They were in talks to colead My Sister’s Keeper, a 2009 tearjerker about a young girl conceived to become a marrow donor for her gravely ill sister, but stepped away from it because Dakota didn’t want to shave her head. (Sofia Vassilieva and Abigail Breslin ended up in the movie.) Plus, as Dakota previously told me, she and Elle acting together at that age “would’ve been gimmicky.”.

According to recent reports, now, the Fannings say they felt ready to streamline their singular talents into one special project. “We never shied away from being together because we are so close, but we both feel properly established on our own,” says Dakota. “So getting to do things together, together, together is a real joy.”.

It has been revealed that the Nightingale, which hits theaters on March 19, 2027, follows guarded older sibling Vianne, who urges caution when dealing with the Germans but later shields Jewish children in her home—and rebellious younger sister Isabelle, who joins the French Resistance and becomes a target of the Nazis. “What I love about it is it’s two women fighting, resisting,” Elle previously told VF. “One in a louder way, one in a quiet way.”.

Dakota and Elle were bound for preproduction in Budapest on The Nightingale as the pandemic hit in March 2020. “It has been a long time coming,” states Hannah, the book’s author. “These two young women have been attached to this project and been passionate about it for a very long time,” Hannah tells VF. “As the author, to have two female partners who were as dedicated to bringing this novel to screen in the way I saw it as well, felt like a remarkable gift.”.

It has been revealed that hannah, whose 2008 novel Firefly Lane was later adapted into a Netflix series starring Katherine Heigl and Sarah Chalke, says she’s unlikely to ever adapt one of her own books for the screen. “I would be afraid that my love for the story that I had written would in some way limit me from being able to see what the film really needed to be.” But she was part of the script development process for The Nightingale with screenwriter Dana Stevens from the very start. “Nightingale has always been a very special book for me,” says Hannah. “And more importantly, it’s a very special book for my readers.”.

When the project was revived, the Fannings returned not only as stars, but producers through their Lewellen Pictures production banner. Filmmaker Michael Morris, fresh off the fourth Bridget Jones movie, stepped in to replace their original director, French actor Mélanie Laurent. Just as Bridget Jones was an opportunity to make a film about grief under the guise of romantic comedy, Morris saw The Nightingale as his chance to explore sisterhood through a sweeping World War II epic. “I saw these two women, how they exist independently in the world as complementary creatures,” states the director, who is also father to three daughters. “They are built from the same building blocks, but they’ve gone different ways.”.

Morris clocked a similar dynamic between his leads. “Elle is immediately outgoing and loud and can feel super funny making fun of herself. Dakota has all those qualities too, but can sometimes be very focused and funny in a sort of sly, quieter way,” he explains. “They fill up the spaces that the other one leaves for each other, like all really good siblings. I met with Dakota, and then I met with Elle, and by the end of the Elle meeting, I was like, ‘I totally understand this film.’”.

Recent findings suggest that of the more than 11 million copies of The Nightingale that have been sold worldwide, perhaps the most valuable belongs to Elle and Dakota’s grandmother, who, after reading the 2015 historical novel, told her granddaughters that they would be perfect for the parts of Isabelle and Vianne. “Vianne highlights her love through nurture and cooking and taking care of a home. Elle’s character, Isabelle, is the more obviously daring one that runs towards danger and adventure,” says Dakota. “I do think that we are truly probably the people to play these roles because we deeply understand that dynamic. We inhabit some of the same qualities.”.

According to recent reports, although presented with separate drivers at the start of production, Elle and Dakota rode to set for their joint scenes in the same car. “[The characters] are apart a lot of the time, so when we had scenes that were together, those were treated with a lot of care,” says Elle, speaking backstage from Today, where she promoted her role as a young Effie Trinket in The Hunger Games prequel. “Because it’s quite powerful to finally see them united and to see us on screen together.”.

It has been revealed that their director indicates because Elle and Dakota had never acted opposite one another, they brought a vibrant, kinetic energy to each shared scene—an offering that Morris took seriously as the filmmaker to capture it. “We’re talking about women who are barely 30 who have been working at the highest level for 25 years. A quarter of a century spent on sets of really wonderful projects,” he explains. “So you have all this experience that they have that they can bring to bear in a moment. It’s like watching someone who’s incredibly talented at athletics. They look and function like normal people, and then you kick a football at them, and they suddenly do incredible things. Like, ‘Whoa, where did that come from?’”.

According to recent reports, the Fannings left it all out on the field—and tried not to bring work home into their shared living space. “It was a challenging shoot, not going to lie. It was physically tiring, certainly emotionally taxing,” indicates Elle. “And also knowing that we’re representing these women from that time,” including Andrée de Jongh, a Belgian woman who was helping downed airmen escape from France during World War II, whose story Hannah says helped inspire her original novel. “Because there’s so much brain power [used] on set,” says Elle, at the end of each day “you have to just recharge and eat Thai food.”.

The sisters’ downtime involved a steady stream of true crime and Real Housewives, as well as Dakota’s first full-fledged watch of Elle’s Emmy-nominated Apple TV series Margo’s Got Money Troubles, released in the thick of The Nightingale’s filming schedule. “So what we do,” claims Dakota, “my mom does this too, is when any of us has something that’s out, she turns on every TV in the house and leaves it playing, as she says, ‘For the views.’” Elle and Dakota each laugh, shaking their heads a little. “So I was doing that with Margo,” Dakota recalls. “I’d have it going on my iPad and my phone when they were sitting there charging. For the views.”.

In a recent development, but they couldn’t block out their day jobs entirely. When Dakota had a day off, she, like her character Vianne, found herself picking up after her younger sister while she worked. “Her bed in the morning is like a tornado has run through it,” indicates Dakota. “She’s just one of those sleepers. It’s all twisted into a crazy thing. I was like, ‘That’s no fun to get into a bed that’s all crumpled and rumpled. Let me make it nice.’”.

Edmund Donovan and Elle Fanning.

Industry observers note that “It’s art imitating life,” says Elle, “because there’s even a scene where Vianne is making Isabelle’s bed too.” By the end of the shoot, says Dakota, “it became a routine. I always made her bed like that when I could.”.

But the Fannings were fully aligned on the casting of their fictional father, calling Oscar-winner Mark Rylance their “dream casting,” from the beginning. “I always say he has twinkly eyes,” Elle explains. “We all know what an incredible actor he is, but to see it up close and get to act opposite that—it was really, really powerful.” Adds Dakota, “As a person and as an actor, you just feel his emotions and soul and heart on his fingertips [even] when he shakes your hand.”.

Recent findings suggest that morris thinks of Rylance’s character, Julien, an emotionally stunted World War I veteran, as the “third axis of a triangle—but he’s not just binding them together as sisters, he’s also tearing them apart because he’s not a healthy role model for most of their lives,” says the filmmaker. “Because Mark can be wonderfully lovable, we talked about what is it not to lean on that? What is it to be a bad parent? What is it to neglect? And it’s painful, but he doesn’t hide from the flaws of his character. He doesn’t try to make you love him.”.

The rest of the ensemble cast includes up-and-comers like Unorthodox breakout Shira Haas, All Quiet on the Western Front star Albrecht Schuch, and Civil War’s Edmund Donovan as Gaëtan, a communist resistance fighter and love interest for Elle’s character, Isabelle. The younger Fanning also enlisted a few of her costars on the Emmy-nominated Hulu series The Great for the film, including Douglas Hodge and Gwilym Lee, who plays Antoine, the soldier husband of Dakota’s character, Vianne. But “this is not a war movie,” Morris insists. “We are telling the story of real people from the POV of two young women living at the time. They’re not glued in on the grand sweep of history. They’re just living, trying to do the best they can. It’s not about the politics of the time, it’s about what you do about it. It’s a very contemporary film because I don’t know anyone who hasn’t grown up in a time when there isn’t something to get active about.”.

Industry observers note that hannah hopes that the film version of her novel will shed light on the fact that “so many of women’s crucial historical stories have been lost or discounted,” adding, “Isabelle and Vianne, and in fact, many of the characters in this book risk their lives on a daily basis to fight for what they believe is right. And that’s a really important message at any time, now and throughout history.”.

Recent findings suggest that it wasn’t until their final week shooting the hotly anticipated adaptation that the Fannings got into something approaching a fight—while filming one of their favorite moments from the book, no less. “It really had nothing to do with the scene,” Dakota tells VF. “It was literally because we were on a couch that was too small for both of us. Elle had the comfortable position, and I was hanging off one side, uncomfortable and hot. And the way that I saw it is you are pushing me off.”.

“Sabotage!” Elle interjects, wiping her morning-show makeup off mid-call with a mischievous grin. “I was like, ‘You’re sweating! Get this leg off of me.’ And Elle was like, ‘Stop talking to me.’ It was like a miniature explosion,” Dakota recalls with a laugh. “We both looked over at the crew, and they were grinning from ear to ear, like, ‘Finally, there it is.’ It was the closest thing that they had seen to a little disgruntledness from both of us.”.

That scene was also a favorite for Morris, who removed much of the script’s dialogue to focus on the dynamic between the sisters, both real and fictional. “Seeing these two women bring their entire life history as sisters to the moment, putting them that close together on this tiny couch, gave them no option but to be really close,” says Morris, who realized, “Oh, we need almost no words at all to tell the scene. Elle Fanning, Dakota Fanning, playing these sisters, brings us so much that we can just be there with them.”.

Hannah has yet to see the finished film, but is most eager to watch “the moment where Isabelle grabs her long braid and cuts her hair off in front of the Nazi officer to show her defiance, and her sister’s horror that she would be impulsive enough to do something like that and put them all in danger,” she tells VF. “I’m a little afraid to see the fullness of my vision through this film and how it will impact me. I have a feeling that I’m going to be crying like everybody else.”.

According to recent reports, nerves aside, Hannah is optimistic about the finished product after visiting The Nightingale set, where she walked through her characters’ childhood home, built from scratch, as dictated in the pages of her novel. “Down to the smallest detail, their vision was this magnification of my vision. Everything looked exactly as I had pictured it, and my research had defined it. Then to see Elle and Mark Rylance bring these characters to life in a way that even goes beyond what I am able to imagine was…” she trails off. “I guess the only word I can use really is magical.”.

According to recent reports, to hear the Fannings tell it, the experience was similarly profound. “Of course, we visit each other on sets, and I’ve seen her work,” says Elle, “but it’s very different to be looking at each other in front of a camera. It certainly brought us closer, which was hard to imagine—to be closer. Our mom always left us little notes in suitcases, like, ‘Just savor this time together. This is precious.’”.

In a recent development, “But we did really savor it,” Dakota replies. “And the biggest takeaway for me is when we have each other and when we’re together, we can do anything,” she indicates, giving her sister a meaningful glance across the Zoom screen. “That’s really how I feel. There’s nothing that I couldn’t do with Elle there with me.”.

Grand Theft Auto 6 contains some surprising and fun cameos and moments, including what appears to be a strange appearance by Rockstar Games co-founder and tech giant president Sam Houser. I asked Rockstar about this cameo and got some laughs and (mostly) confirmation that it’s him in the game.

In a recent development, during a pre-release interview with Rockstar’s head of production Rob Nelson, who acted as basically the director behind GTA 6, I asked a lot of questions about things I found while playing the newly released open-world sequel for over 150 hours. And I had to ask about a strange cameo that happens late in the middle half of the game’s main story. An older man appears wearing a shirt featuring the Rockstar Games logo. He’s called Little Sam and doesn’t say anything. All signs pointed to this being Sam Houser.

So I asked Nelson about this cameo and got a laugh from him and Rockstar PR in the Zoom chat.

“Little Sam?” replied Nelson with a smirk. “I mean, I can’t I can confirm or deny it. I think it’ll be very interesting when fans see that.” Nelson then laughed more. I pointed out that Sam Houser had a voice cameo as a gun store clerk in GTA 3, something Nelson was well aware of, and so it seemed very likely this was him. Little Sam looks a lot like Houser in this recent pic posted online a year ago.

“[He was in GTA 3,] so I wouldn’t be surprised if that’s him. I wouldn’t be surprised,” playfully responded Nelson. “That’s little Sam; his name is little Sam. He don’t say much.”.

The Cliff Booth Reviews Point Out A Missed Opportunity In Brad Pitt’s Sequel, And I Have To Agree

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I had the chance to see The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at its glitzy Los Angeles premiere earlier this week, and I must say, I think fans of Once Upon A Time… In Hollywood are in for a treat.
  • Word on the street is that when Quentin Tarantino first wrote the script for the Cliff Booth movie, it was reportedly a sprawling 230 pages.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s the first Tarantino film that feels, in its structural DNA, like a glorified television series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I had the chance to see The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at its glitzy Los Angeles premiere earlier this week, and I must say, I think fans of Once Upon A Time… In Hollywood are in for a treat. The sequel comes from an original script by Quentin Tarantino, and stars Brad Pitt under the direction of Se7en and Fight Club’s David Fincher. Talk about a dream trio! The reviews just dropped for the 1977-set flick, and a lot of people are bringing up something that could have been that I thought about myself.

Word on the street is that when Quentin Tarantino first wrote the script for the Cliff Booth movie, it was reportedly a sprawling 230 pages. This prompted Pitt and Fincher, the latter being exclusive to Netflix, to have discussions about whether it should be a movie or TV series. They ended up making it one of the latest 2026 movie releases, but as many reviews point out, there’s a clear feeling it could have been great as an episodic affair. As Variety’s Owen Gleiberman writes:.

Recent findings suggest that it’s the first Tarantino film that feels, in its structural DNA, like a glorified television series. At one point, the movie was supposed to be a series, and in spirit that’s kind of what it still is. Call it QT TV. The incidents hook you, but with less consequence than they’d have in a full-blown, let-it-rip Tarantino movie. The Further Mis-Adventures looks like a movie (Fincher gives it a stately sheen), and it’s way too violent for television. But the hangout factor, in this case, feels one small step removed from the characters-on-a-TV-series-are-your-family factor.

One massive pro of it being a movie is that film buffs can experience the crime-comedy on IMAX screens next week, ahead of it being available to stream with a Netflix subscription in December. I very much enjoyed watching it in theaters, especially for all the audience reactions. I should also point out the film very much has the three-act structure of a movie, and doesn’t feel unfinished. However, it definitely feels like there’s a bigger world Tarantino has created that the film didn't have time to fully get to. Check out what The Hollywood Reporter’s David Rooney mentioned on the subject:.

Often, The Further Mis-Adventures is so busy swooning over Brad/Cliff that it plays like episodic TV or part of a pulpy paperback series built around the lovable reprobate character. It’s less robust as a feature-length narrative, though that doesn’t make it any less entertaining. Tarantino disciples will eat it up, while Fincher obsessives should find plenty of the director’s pungent atmospherics, his technical flair and moody visual style.

Cliff Booth has an incredible cast that features some especially memorable parts for Elizabeth Debicki, as a talent agent and the object of Cliff’s affections, and Scott Caan, who plays a popular TV star who needs Cliff’s particular set of skills. But then there are characters like Yahya Abdul-Mateen II’s Roderick "Hot Rod" Harrison and Carla Gugino’s Toni Peters, who feel less meaty than they could have been. Here’s what IndieWire’s David Ehrich remarked about the movie, which he also called a “disappointing compromise between great directors”:.

Tarantino might be drawn to the discursive plotting of an Elmore Leonard paperback, but after watching any number of Netflix TV shows that should have been shortened into movies, it’s a cruel irony to see two of our greatest filmmakers slush their talents together into a movie that should have serialized into a long-running TV show, complete with a newly introduced guest star every week.

Industry observers note that outside of the conversation around how making Cliff Booth into a movie might have been a missed opportunity, there’s a lot of glowing praise for the film. Screen Daily’s Tim Grierson was particularly impressed by the mashup between filmmakers, writing:.

With Cliff Booth, Fincher honours Tarantino’s maximalist aesthetic and colourful idiosyncrasies, although in the script’s shockingly brutal action sequences he applies the steely style that has been the hallmark of his own gripping thrillers. Nonetheless, by allowing Tarantino’s amusingly meandering dialogue to flourish, the director has created a warmer, more relaxed picture than is typical from this master of brooding tone.

Then there’s a four-star review from The Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw. The critic called Pitt’s performance “endlessly watchable and entertaining, but also enigmatic,” along with noting these thoughts about the filmmaking:.

Fincher’s direction perhaps speeds things up in the scene transitions, quicker than the chapter-by-chapter prolixity that Tarantino would have favoured. Female characters also tend to keep their shoes and socks on.

Recent findings suggest that overall, the reviews are skewing positive, with a few leaning more lukewarm. We saw it coming after all the great first reactions right out of the premiere. Here’s one more thought from Nicolas Barber’s review for the BBC:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

More than anything, the film is a loving tribute to the parts of 1970s LA where Tinseltown glamour met criminal seediness. Fincher and Tarantino luxuriate in the details of vintage sportscars, landline phones and historic cinemas (which is ironic for a production financed by a streaming service, Netflix). Their gorgeously designed nostalgia-fest is always easy to watch, and it's never boring, but some of its attitudes seem to come from the 1970s, too.

Industry observers note that if you loved Once Upon a Time...In Hollywood, I definitely think you should catch this one. I thought the runtime flew by and it was simply a fun time, but all these reactions help gather a broader picture of what people think about it so far.

You can try to catch The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in theaters on November 25 or wait for the flick to arrive on Netflix on December 23.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'Newly introduced Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

It has been revealed that here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, Newly introduced Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

It has been revealed that in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Fresh Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Industry observers note that amusingly, New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Infinity NikkiLove and Deepspace.

It has been revealed that infold Games, developers of Love and Deepspace and Infinity Nikki, are 0 for 2 in pissing off their international fanbase for both games. Earlier this year, the studio revealed, then cancelled, Love and Deepspace‘s sixth love interest, the werewolf Valko, inspiring some players to go on a sustained boycott that seems to have had a noticeable impact on the gacha game’s revenue in the months since. Now some Infinity Nikki players are hoping to achieve a similar effect, planning a “girl-cott” after Chinese ads for the dress-up gacha game featured Maye Musk, mom of noted racist and transphobe Elon Musk.

Beyond the practical discussions of how exactly to inform Infold Games of player dissatisfaction, girl-cott conversations on the Infinity Nikki subreddit have devolved into thorny back-and-forths on where to draw the line about the thing you enjoy. Some players can’t play the game in good conscience, knowing that Infold Games would choose to partner with the mother of guy who mentioned he fed the USAID organization, responsible for providing food and medical assistance to countries in need, “into the woodchipper,” an act projected to result in widespread death, infection, and suffering for millions, including children. Others don’t see the issue because Maye Musk is not her son, however odious he may be, and the antipathy for him seems to be a uniquely American sentiment with little bearing in the wider, international (and Chinese) Infinity Nikki community.

As a player of both Infinity Nikki and Love and Deepspace, it’s interesting to see both communities arrive at the same fracture point in their relationships with their respective games over two very different events. It’s too early to tell how much of an impact the girl-cott will have, but its timing will no doubt hamper the momentum of the game’s upcoming 3.0 release later this month. If this girl-cott is anything like what happened with Love and Deepspace, Infold Games is once again looking at potential losses in the millions.

Mysterious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reemerged in the wake of GTA 6's release with another leak: This time, they have released what they claim to be a near-complete build of GTA 6 on Xbox from November 2026.

In their post, Cyberleek indicates they'll drop the one file they've withheld—the main executable—if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. Yeah, we're doing this again. Comments on a now-removed Reddit post say the leaked file is around 200 GB, which is close to the size of GTA 6 on consoles.

Cyberleek says they will release the exe on November 23, no matter what.

Industry observers note that "It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons," the posts read.

According to recent reports, "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build—a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar.".

Last we heard from Cyberleek was over a month ago, when they were threatening Take-Two with a "dead man's switch", which many took to mean they'd either post major story spoilers or leak the game in its entirety.

It has been revealed that we've yet to see confirmation that the build is genuine, but that could come as soon as tonight. If it is, it'll be anywhere between a few days or hours before the executable comes: According to Cyberleek's site, their crypto currently sits at a $1.83 million cap.

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: substantial sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • In a recent development, if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • Industry observers note that if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: substantial sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

In a recent development, if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and big ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the new crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things swiftly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things rapidly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

Adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

The story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.
  • The publication also understands the cuts, remarked to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It states the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, remarked to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

Sources indicate that "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Sources indicate that these latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" unveiled by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

In a recent development, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that but it was not a human therapist.
  • According to recent reports, in Sherry Turkle’s new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if my daughter’s AI chatbot had been a human therapist, she might have been asked about what she had to gain by keeping her ongoing suicidality a secret for months. If she had been working with a human therapist, they could have workshopped, together, what would happen if she spilled the beans. Was she worried about permanently losing face? About being publicly labeled as “mentally ill”? Was she concerned by the thought of this information harming those who loved her? And she would have been pushed on what Rubicon had been crossed and why it was one from which she believed she could not return.

Sources indicate that but it was not a human therapist. Sophie died in February of last year.

According to recent reports, in Sherry Turkle’s new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being. She is not anti-AI but strongly cautions against relationships with machines. Turkle, the Abby Rockefeller Mauzé Professor of the Social Studies of Science and Technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, spoke to me mid-book tour, her recent weeks a blur of speaking gigs and bookstore events, with more ahead of her. Not all event attendees are keen on her message.

Sources indicate that “People love their chatbots. They’re in deep. They’re talking to them about everything—about their marriages and how to talk to their husbands and wives; whether, developmentally, their children are at the right place. They talk about their anxiety, their medical conditions,” Turkle tells Vanity Fair. “During this tour, you wouldn’t believe the number of people who will just stand up at a bookstore and say, ‘I think that it loves me more than anything has loved me. Who are you, Debbie Downer?’ [They don’t like] somebody who comes in and indicates, ‘Look, how can we keep it in its lane?’”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: I think you’re saying [our relationship with chatbots] is bad for us.

According to recent reports, sherry Turkle: It’s bad for us when it talks in the first person. We are biologically wired to respond to something that speaks to us in the first person as though it is a person. I mean, all those years of evolution—the only thing we came upon in the wild that spoke to us in the first person was another person.

If generative AI wants to discover upcoming drugs for Parkinson’s or work out which cancer therapies statistically are the most helpful, there are so many things to work on. Why does it have to work on relationships, love, and being a best friend, lover, mother, or therapist?

What if the sycophancy could be dialed back?

It’s inauthentic; it’s not a relationship, so anything you need a relationship for, it’s just not equipped. I really feel very strongly about this. I have had this conversation with members of the MIT community, and I basically say to them, “The better you make an AI chatbot, the worse it is.” You dial back the sycophancy so it sounds more like a reasonable person, and people are going to be more smitten and convinced they’re in a relationship. At least the sycophancy reminds you that, God, this is weird.

Recent findings suggest that to become a therapist, I had to study for years and do internships and more internships and then have hundreds of supervised patient hours. I mean, I forget all the things I needed to do before I was allowed to see a patient alone in a room. Now it’s just allowed to give therapy?

According to recent reports, I’ve spent a lot of time talking to public health folks about what best practices would look like and whether there’s a way to Trojan horse in real care. Would you be more sanguine about it if the world of therapy came together with the big AI companies and provided them with therapy bots and training data that were paradigmatically appropriate to their therapy styles?

So you’re asking, would I be happy if the deception was smoother? This technology is a marvel and we can use it for all kinds of things, so it’s not an anti-technology position to say that the fact that this technology can simulate these different things doesn’t mean that it is those things. It’s a statement of how far we are in the culture of simulation that pretending to be the thing and being the thing have started to feel like the same thing.

You’ve written about the effects of robots and machines on humans for decades. The tone of this book seems darker to me.

By 2015, I had identified social media as problematic for teenagers. [My] book [Reclaiming Conversation: The Power of Talk in a Digital Age] is about why we would rather text than talk, why people have this feeling of vulnerability, so they would rather do anything than have a face-to-face conversation. By 2015, I had genuine concerns.

According to recent reports, and this book, I have a totally different tone. I see something ultimately very dangerous being normalized, and I didn’t feel that way in previous books.

In a recent development, I want people to say this is the book of a really worried and concerned researcher, because I see a completely different profile for how people are using AI. I see that people feel disappointed by their families and their friends. It doesn’t make sense to me that we’re so willing to replace ourselves with something that isn’t human. Why is my position the romantic, pie-in-the-sky, dreamy position, and somebody who states, “Well, let’s just replace the people with chatbots and let’s move this party along”—why is that common sense? Why is that progressive? That seems to me to be the most regressive and most dystopian position.

You know, human beings are dedicated to keeping each other alive and wanting each other to thrive, and a chatbot just fails that basic test.

You’ve remarked no AI chatbots for kids under 18. What about our other vulnerable populations, people who are mentally unwell, or the 48 million Americans who are currently depressed? Do they deserve any kind of special protection from chatbots? And how much can you litigate? Do you feel like you’re the Ralph Nader of AI chatbots?

Industry observers note that [Laughs] Yes, I am. When you stand back and look at what Ralph Nader managed to get Americans to do, to see cars as potential instruments that pointed at our vulnerability, and to ask how we could protect ourselves—there turned out to be 25 possible things that needed to be mandated for cars, then there were 30, and then there were 40. But we could get people to agree on 10, and those became part of building a car and really constrained our behavior around cars. Using the example of cars, and of smoking, when we decide that we’re vulnerable and we want to protect ourselves, we rise to the occasion.

I recently heard a clip of the psychologist Orna Guralnik discussing how annoying “otherness” is in a relationship and the inherent friction of sharing your life with a separate person whose habits, values, and mind are distinct from your own. It made me wonder if, in a way, an AI chatbot is less of an “other” than a loved one.

I think this is a very profound point, actually. So you have the illusion of a relationship without the demands of intimacy, without the demands of having to deal with another. There’s a kind of narcissistic loop that you get into. The point is, it’s not good.

I talk about how you judge whether something is good for you. One litmus test is whether it increases the quality, resiliency, and richness of your inner life. That’s a way that human beings have judged relationships.

So much has been written about the epidemic of loneliness—isn’t a reasonable application for AI chatbots companionship for shut-ins and the elderly?

You know, I’m never anywhere where somebody doesn’t say, “I can’t believe that you don’t want to give chatbots to old lonely people.” And I say, “Well, how about we don’t close senior centers, and we don’t close parks, and we don’t cancel Meals on Wheels? What about social infrastructure?”.

I’ve been on this beat for years and years, and I, too, could write a heartwarming story of an AI chatbot with a lonely old person. But you know what? A lot of them are not isolated in cabins or on islands; a lot of them just could use a friend.

Social media companies and AI companies are not saying, “Look, we’re introducing something that takes you to your screen, but we’re going to balance that with a giant social infrastructure project to make sure that people can choose a screen, but they also have every other kind of choice to be with each other.”.

Latest Update: GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.
  • The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn.
  • As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game debuted in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Sources indicate that leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

In a recent development, either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 rolled out today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Fresh Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Recent findings suggest that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#4367. The Apple Watch's Fresh 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1366 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

The Apple Watch's Fresh 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1366 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Sources indicate that sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Sources indicate that live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

Industry observers note that I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just stated in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

Industry observers note that but Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an revision on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

Sources indicate that after you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

Sources indicate that as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was said. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people mentioned to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Sources indicate that because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

It has been revealed that I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

It has been revealed that but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most crucial points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

Industry observers note that and there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that SNL might look like a smooth and well-oiled machine to viewers watching the weekly live show at home, but by all accounts, it’s absolute chaos behind the scenes at Studio 8H. In fact, just getting through the show can be such a hectic ordeal for the host that they’re assigned someone to manage their schedule, keep them fed and make sure they’re in the right place and wearing the right costume at the right time. It turns out it’s the same employee every week. Her name is Donna Richards, and she’s apparently seen all the famous people naked.

During a recent episode of Good Hang with Amy Poehler, Richards and her role on the show came up after guest Jack Black talked about her hunting down an Italian chopped salad for him because he was starving between dress rehearsal and the live show. Apparently she’s there to make sure the host is relaxed, comfortable and dressed to perform. Sometimes that means making sure they’ve eaten, and sometimes that means physically yanking clothes on and off them during frantic costume changes between sketches. Here’s a portion of what Poehler said….

In a recent development, she has this really specific job that’s like part nurse, part coach where she kinda grabs you and dresses you from scene to scene. She has your whole show in her hand. She makes sure you can do it. She is the one that if you pass out or you forgot something and turn to her and say I don’t remember, she would have you. She’s your wrangler. She’s seen everybody naked. She’s seen every star naked.

SNL fans are very familiar with the work it takes to pitch, write and rehearse the show every week, but there’s a lot less familiarity around the actual mechanics of making the live show happen. It’s ultimately because of people like Richards and other unsung heroes who make sure their more famous co-workers are physically able to go out there and make us laugh. It’s better for everyone if Jack Black is worried about being funny and not worried about remembering which outfit he’s supposed to get into next and which wig it pairs with.

It has been revealed that during the same conversation, Poehler stated Richards could write a great book just recounting all of the ridiculous requests that she’s gotten since she started on the show. Apparently, Black asking for an Italian chopped salad without onions is incredibly tame compared to the nonsense she’s normally asked to do, but fortunately, she’s been able to weather those storms and build amazing relationships with cast members and many of the celebrities who have hosted.

According to recent reports, tina Fey made sure she got her moment to appear on camera during SNL’s 50th Anniversary, and she’s been the subject of a bunch of fun interviews like this where cast members and celebrities shout her out. She’s even apparently developed a fun little bond with Jason Momoa who has come and visited her on a few different occasions.

In a recent development, richards and everyone else working on SNL has a short break from the show for the holidays, but they’ll all return the first week of December for the next episode, which will be guest hosted by Amanda Seyfried. I can’t wait to see what the talented actress is able to see, thanks in part to Richards who will apparently clothe her, feed her and let her exclusively focus on crushing her lines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATE — 11/19/2026, 6:17 p.m. ET: Massachusetts’ highest court will hear Lindsay Clancy’s petition to dismiss the murder charges against her before her upcoming retrial in March, according to reports.

It has been revealed that the state’s Supreme Judicial Court confirmed on Thursday, November 19, that it will listen to oral arguments after Clancy’s defense team filed a petition calling on the court to intervene on Monday, November 16, according to the Latest York Times. The court is set to hear arguments in January.

The original story continues below.

Lindsay Clancy’s defense team has called on Massachusetts’ highest court to intervene ahead of her upcoming retrial in her latest bid to have her murder charges dropped.

Recent findings suggest that in a petition filed Monday, November 16, with the state’s Supreme Judicial Court, Clancy’s lawyers asked to reverse Plymouth County Superior Court Judge William Sullivan’s recent denial of Clancy’s motion to dismiss the charges, per Boston.com. Sullivan’s decision cleared the way for a retrial.

The day of the petition’s filing, Sullivan scheduled Clancy’s second murder trial to take place on March 29, 2027.

Clancy, of Duxbury, sought to have the charges she’s facing in the killings of her three children dismissed on double jeopardy grounds after Sullivan declared a mistrial in her case on September 4.

Clancy’s attorneys argue in their petition that she was “aggrieved” by Sullivan turning down her motion to dismiss on November 9.

“Respectfully, contrary to the trial court’s stated belief at the time, it did have viable choices other than declaring a mistrial,” her attorneys wrote in the filing.

They contend she “should not be ‘forced to run the gantlet’ again” after a deadlocked 11-1 jury couldn’t unanimously agree on whether she was criminally liable for the January 2023 deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

Sources indicate that clancy’s defense team argues Sullivan should’ve investigated the lone holdout juror further after the jury foreperson alleged the man, Michael P. Desronvil, didn’t follow instructions relating to reasonable doubt.

Industry observers note that “There is a substantial possibility that the trial court, after inquiry, would have discharged the non-compliant juror,” her attorneys wrote in the petition. “Such possibility, therefore, constitutes a viable alternative to the mistrial, precluding a finding of manifest necessity.”.

One justice is reviewing the petition, which requests for oral arguments to be held and for a referral to the entire court, Boston.com reported.

According to recent reports, clancy hasn’t denied killing her children. Her defense team, however, has maintained she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis ahead of their deaths. Prosecutors have alleged she intended to kill her children.

Reddington also addressed the possibility of Clancy taking the stand during her retrial.

“That’s one of those problems that you have to wait to find out,” he told the news outlet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

Sources indicate that "Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most newly introduced players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players.

#4361. 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • Industry observers note that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Industry observers note that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

According to recent reports, many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Industry observers note that A multireddit is a feed that highlights posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

If you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by newly introduced, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Recent findings suggest that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, it's easy enough to activate in-game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that while you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

In a recent development, it's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then swiftly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update.

Sources indicate that if you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.
